Purpose: Verify that the log parsers implement the documented formats of the servers the base paper used, and measure their throughput.

Validation Status.Tested Against: synthetic lines written to each format's documented syntax
Validation Status.Not Tested Against: live capture from a running Samba server, auditd host or Windows endpoint
Known Gaps: syslog year is absent in RFC3164 and is inferred as the current year, so logs spanning 31 December parse with a one-year jump
multi-host interleaving assumes monotonic timestamps within a source; a clock skew between hosts can order windows wrongly
non-UTF8 paths and filenames with embedded pipes are not decoded
truncated or rotated log lines are skipped rather than partially recovered
Validation Status.Conclusion: The parsers implement the documented formats and produce the same window schema as the trace generator, so real and emulated data share one pipeline. They have not been validated against production traffic and should be treated as unproven against real logs until they are.

Base Paper Comparison.Paper: Fluent Bit -> InfluxDB -> CSV -> one-second aggregation (Sect. 3.2, 4.2)
Base Paper Comparison.This Project: watchdog observer for live monitoring; ml.ingest for offline replay of Samba, auditd, Windows and Sysmon logs into the same window schema
Base Paper Comparison.Still Absent: an InfluxDB time-series backend and a Fluent Bit forwarder; see docker/smb-testbed for a provisioning scaffold that was authored but not executed in this environment
